content: Certainly. 1. Amoxicillin and Acyclovir: Co-administration may lead to increased levels of either drug due to reduced renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely for potential interactions. 2. Amoxicillin and Allopurinol: Allopurinol may reduce the toxicity of amoxicillin. However, it can increase the likelihood of allergic or hypersensitivity reactions to amoxicillin. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Amoxicillin and Aspirin: Concurrent use may increase the levels of either drug by competing for plasma protein binding or by reducing renal clearance. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Amoxicillin and Aspirin Rectal: Similar to oral aspirin, rectal administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor the patient. 5. Amoxicillin and Aspirin/Citric Acid/Sodium Bicarbonate: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Amoxicillin and Methotrexate: Amoxicillin can increase methotrexate levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially leading to hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity. Monitor serum methotrexate concentrations and assess for toxicity. 7. Amoxicillin and Oral Contraceptives (e.g., Ethinyl Estradiol, Levonorgestrel): Amoxicillin may reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional or alternative contraceptive methods may be advisable during concurrent use. Monitor for reduced contraceptive efficacy. 8. Amoxicillin and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., Atezolizumab, Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab): Amoxicillin may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 9. Amoxicillin and Tetracyclines (e.g., Doxycycline, Minocycline): Tetracyclines may antagonize the bactericidal action of amoxicillin. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. If used together, monitor for reduced efficacy of amoxicillin. 10. Amoxicillin and Live Vaccines (e.g., Typhoid, Cholera, BCG): Amoxicillin may reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 11. Amoxicillin and Warfarin: Amoxicillin may enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin by affecting vitamin K metabolism. Monitor coagulation parameters closely and adjust warfarin dosage as needed. 12. Amoxicillin and Methyclothiazide/Metolazone: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 13. Amoxicillin and Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Antibiotics like amoxicillin may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Monitor for reduced efficacy of the bowel preparation. 14. Amoxicillin and Sulfasalazine: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by competing for plasma protein binding or reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor the patient. 15. Amoxicillin and Pexidartinib: Both drugs may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. Monitor liver function closely if co-administration is necessary. 16. Amoxicillin and Pretomanid: Co-administration may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents during treatment. Monitor liver function tests closely. 17. Amoxicillin and Azithromycin/Clarithromycin/Erythromycin: Macrolides may reduce the efficacy of amoxicillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of amoxicillin. 18. Amoxicillin and Aztreonam: These agents may exhibit synergistic effects against Enterobacteriaceae. This combination may be used therapeutically in specific infections. 19. Amoxicillin and Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6): Amoxicillin may reduce the levels of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. Monitor for potential vitamin B6 deficiency during prolonged therapy. 20. Amoxicillin and Rose Hips/Salicylates (Non-ASA): Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor the patient. 21. Amoxicillin and Willow Bark: Similar to salicylates, co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 22. Amoxicillin and Patiramer: Patiramer may bind to amoxicillin in the gastrointestinal tract, potentially reducing its absorption. Administer the drugs at least 2 hours apart and monitor for reduced antibiotic efficacy. 23. Amoxicillin and Bendroflumethiazide/Chlorothiazide: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 24. Amoxicillin and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., Camrelizumab, Cemiplimab, Dostarlimab): Amoxicillin may interfere with the therapeutic effects of these agents through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 25. Amoxicillin and Estradiol/Mestranol: Amoxicillin may reduce the levels of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, additional contraceptive measures may be advisable during concurrent use. 26. Amoxicillin and Sodium Phenylacetate: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 27. Amoxicillin and Salsalate: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug by competing for plasma protein binding. Use caution and monitor the patient. 28. Amoxicillin and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., Sintilimab, Toripalimab): Amoxicillin may interfere with the therapeutic effects of these agents through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 29. Amoxicillin and Methotrexate: Co-administration may increase methotrexate levels, leading to potential toxicity. Monitor serum methotrexate levels and assess for hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity. 30. Amoxicillin and Warfarin: Amoxicillin may enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin. Monitor coagulation parameters closely and adjust warfarin dosage as needed.
